summary.short: Virginia's Consumer Data Protection Act regulates businesses that control or process personal data of Virginia residents above volume thresholds: consumer rights of access, correction, deletion, portability and opt-out; controller and processor duties, including data protection assessments and children's protections; exclusive Attorney General enforcement. Effective 1 January 2023.
summary.long: The Act (Code of Virginia §§ 59.1-575 to 59.1-584) applies to persons conducting business in Virginia or targeting its residents that, in a calendar year, control or process personal data of at least 100,000 consumers, or of at least 25,000 consumers while deriving over 50 percent of gross revenue from selling personal data. Public bodies, GLBA financial institutions, HIPAA covered entities and business associates, nonprofits and higher-education institutions are excluded, as are listed health, credit-reporting, FERPA, employment and other data. Consumers may confirm and access, correct, delete and port their data and opt out of targeted advertising, sale and profiling for significant decisions; controllers answer within 45 days and run an appeal process. Controllers must limit collection, secure data, obtain consent for sensitive data, not sell precise geolocation data, give privacy notices, restrict processing of known children's data and conduct data protection assessments for high-risk processing. Processors act under binding contracts. Social media platforms must screen for users under 16 and limit their use to one hour a day unless a parent consents. The Attorney General enforces exclusively, after a 30-day cure notice, with injunctions and civil penalties up to $7,500 per violation; there is no private right of action.

obligations.summary: Controllers must comply with authenticated consumer requests to confirm processing and access data, correct inaccuracies, delete data, obtain a portable copy, and opt out of targeted advertising, sale and profiling for decisions with legal or similarly significant effects; a parent may act for a known child.
obligations.conditional_on: Request authenticated with commercially reasonable efforts (§ 59.1-577 B 4); exemptions for de-identified and pseudonymous data (§ 59.1-581 C-D) and the limitations in § 59.1-582

evidence.quote: A controller shall comply with an authenticated consumer request to exercise the right:

obligations.summary: Controllers must answer requests within 45 days (one 45-day extension with notice), explain any refusal with appeal instructions, and respond free of charge up to twice a year per consumer; controllers that obtained data from third parties may satisfy deletion by keeping a suppression record or opting the consumer out.

evidence.quote: a controller shall comply with a request by a consumer to exercise the consumer rights authorized pursuant to subsection A as follows:

obligations.summary: Controllers must establish a conspicuously available appeal process for refused requests, decide appeals in writing with reasons within 60 days, and, if the appeal is denied, give the consumer a way to submit a complaint to the Attorney General.

evidence.quote: A controller shall establish a process for a consumer to appeal the controller's refusal to take action on a request within a reasonable period of time

obligations.summary: Controllers must offer, and describe in the privacy notice, secure and reliable means to submit rights requests, and may not require a new account to exercise rights.

evidence.quote: A controller shall establish, and shall describe in a privacy notice, one or more secure and reliable means for consumers to submit a request to exercise their consumer rights under this chapter.

obligations.summary: Controllers must limit collection to what is adequate, relevant and reasonably necessary for the disclosed purposes, and may not process data for purposes neither necessary to nor compatible with those disclosed purposes without consent (consent as second character).

evidence.quote: Limit the collection of personal data to what is adequate, relevant, and reasonably necessary in relation to the purposes for which such data is processed, as disclosed to the consumer

obligations.summary: Controllers must establish, implement and maintain reasonable administrative, technical and physical data security practices appropriate to the volume and nature of the data.

evidence.quote: Establish, implement, and maintain reasonable administrative, technical, and physical data security practices to protect the confidentiality, integrity, and accessibility of personal data.

obligations.summary: Controllers may not process data in violation of anti-discrimination laws or discriminate (deny goods, charge different prices, lower quality) against consumers who exercise their rights; differential offers tied to opt-outs or bona fide loyalty programs remain allowed.

evidence.quote: A controller shall not discriminate against a consumer for exercising any of the consumer rights contained in this chapter, including denying goods or services, charging different prices or rates for goods or services, or providing a different level of quality of goods and services to the consumer.

obligations.summary: Controllers may not process sensitive data without the consumer's consent; sensitive data of a known child must be processed in accordance with COPPA.

evidence.quote: Not process sensitive data concerning a consumer without obtaining the consumer's consent

obligations.summary: Controllers may not sell or offer for sale a consumer's precise geolocation data (added by Acts 2026, c. 820, per text comparison).

evidence.quote: Not sell or offer for sale precise geolocation data concerning a consumer.

obligations.summary: Controllers must give consumers a reasonably accessible, clear and meaningful privacy notice listing data categories, purposes, how to exercise and appeal rights, data shared with third parties and the categories of those third parties.

evidence.quote: Controllers shall provide consumers with a reasonably accessible, clear, and meaningful privacy notice that includes:

obligations.summary: Controllers that sell personal data or process it for targeted advertising must clearly and conspicuously disclose this and how consumers can opt out.
obligations.conditional_on: Controller sells personal data to third parties or processes it for targeted advertising

evidence.quote: If a controller sells personal data to third parties or processes personal data for targeted advertising, the controller shall clearly and conspicuously disclose such processing, as well as the manner in which a consumer may exercise the right to opt out of such processing.

obligations.summary: Without parental consent under COPPA, controllers may not process a known child's personal data for targeted advertising, sale or significant-decision profiling, beyond what is reasonably necessary for the online service, for undisclosed or incompatible purposes, or for longer than necessary.
obligations.conditional_on: Personal data collected from a known child (under 13); parental consent per COPPA (§ 59.1-578 F 3)

evidence.quote: Subject to the consent requirement established by subdivision 3, no controller shall process any personal data collected from a known child:

obligations.summary: Without parental consent under COPPA, controllers may not collect a known child's precise geolocation data unless reasonably necessary for the online service, only for the time necessary, and while showing the child a signal that collection is under way.

evidence.quote: no controller shall collect precise geolocation data from a known child unless (i) such precise geolocation data is reasonably necessary for the controller to provide an online service, product, or feature

obligations.summary: Controllers or processors operating a social media platform must use commercially reasonable methods, such as a neutral age screen, to determine whether a user is under 16, and must treat a user as a minor when the user's device or browser signals so.

evidence.quote: Any controller or processor that operates a social media platform shall (i) use commercially reasonable methods, such as a neutral age screen mechanism, to determine whether a user is a minor

obligations.summary: Social media platform operators must limit minors' use to one hour per day per service or application, and let a parent give verifiable parental consent to raise or lower the limit (without extra parental access to the minor's data or accounts).

evidence.quote: limit a minor's use of such social media platform to one hour per day, per service or application

obligations.summary: Information collected to determine a user's age may be used only for age determination and age-appropriate experiences.

evidence.quote: Information collected for the purpose of determining a user's age shall not be used for any purpose other than age determination and provision of age-appropriate experiences.

obligations.summary: Social media platform operators may not withhold, degrade or raise the price of any online service, product or feature because they cannot provide use beyond the one-hour limit; offers reasonably related to compliance remain allowed.

evidence.quote: No controller or processor that operates a social media platform shall withhold, degrade, lower the quality of, or increase the price of any online service, product, or feature to a user

obligations.summary: Processors must follow the controller's instructions and assist it with consumer requests, security and breach notification under § 18.2-186.6, and information for data protection assessments.

evidence.quote: A processor shall adhere to the instructions of a controller and shall assist the controller in meeting its obligations under this chapter.

obligations.summary: Controller-processor processing must be governed by a binding contract setting out instructions, nature, purpose, data types, duration and rights, and requiring processor confidentiality, deletion or return of data, compliance information, cooperation with assessments (or an independent assessor's report; audit as second character) and flow-down to subcontractors.

evidence.quote: A contract between a controller and a processor shall govern the processor's data processing procedures with respect to processing performed on behalf of the controller.

obligations.summary: Controllers must conduct and document data protection assessments, weighing benefits against risks to consumers, for targeted advertising, sale of personal data, risky profiling, sensitive data and other heightened-risk processing; one assessment may cover comparable operations and assessments made under other laws may count.
obligations.conditional_on: Processing activities created or generated after 2023-01-01 (§ 59.1-580 G)

evidence.quote: A controller shall conduct and document a data protection assessment of each of the following processing activities involving personal data:

obligations.summary: Controllers offering an online service, product or feature directed to consumers they actually know are children must conduct a data protection assessment covering its purpose, the categories of children's data processed and the processing purposes.

evidence.quote: Each controller that offers any online service, product, or feature directed to consumers whom such controller has actual knowledge are children shall conduct a data protection assessment for such online service, product, or feature

obligations.summary: On a civil investigative demand, controllers must make relevant data protection assessments available to the Attorney General; assessments stay confidential and exempt from FOIA, and disclosure does not waive privilege.
obligations.conditional_on: Attorney General request under a civil investigative demand relevant to an investigation

evidence.quote: the controller shall make the data protection assessment available to the Attorney General

obligations.summary: Controllers holding de-identified data must take reasonable measures against re-association, publicly commit not to re-identify it and contractually bind recipients to the chapter; controllers disclosing pseudonymous or de-identified data must oversee recipients' contractual compliance.

evidence.quote: Publicly commit to maintaining and using de-identified data without attempting to re-identify the data

obligations.summary: Data processed under the § 59.1-582 exemptions may be used only for the listed purposes, must be necessary, proportionate and limited to them, and must be protected by reasonable security measures; the controller bears the burden of showing the exemption applies.

evidence.quote: Personal data processed by a controller pursuant to this section shall not be processed for any purpose other than those expressly listed in this section unless otherwise allowed by this chapter.

obligations.summary: Before initiating any action, the Attorney General must give the controller or processor 30 days' written notice identifying the provisions allegedly violated; no action follows a cure with an express written statement.

evidence.quote: Prior to initiating any action under this chapter, the Attorney General shall provide a controller or processor 30 days' written notice identifying the specific provisions of this chapter the Attorney General alleges have been or are being violated.

obligations.summary: The Attorney General may issue civil investigative demands (procedure of § 59.1-9.10) when it has reasonable cause to believe a person is violating or about to violate the chapter.

evidence.quote: the Attorney General is empowered to issue a civil investigative demand

enforcement.authority: Attorney General of Virginia (exclusive enforcement), by action in the name of the Commonwealth
enforcement.triggered_by: Continued violation of the chapter after the 30-day cure period, or breach of the express written statement given to the Attorney General
enforcement.max_penalty_text: civil penalties of up to $7,500 for each violation under this chapter
enforcement.penalty_formula: Up to $7,500 per violation; penalties, expenses and attorney fees go to the Regulatory, Consumer Advocacy, Litigation, and Enforcement Revolving Trust Fund
enforcement.cure_period: 30 days after the Attorney General's written notice; no action if the controller or processor cures and gives an express written statement that violations are cured and will not recur

evidence.quote: the Attorney General may initiate an action in the name of the Commonwealth and may seek an injunction to restrain any violations of this chapter and civil penalties of up to $7,500 for each violation under this chapter.

enforcement.authority: Attorney General of Virginia (exclusive enforcement), by action in the name of the Commonwealth
enforcement.triggered_by: Continued violation of the chapter after the 30-day cure period, or breach of the express written statement
enforcement.cure_period: 30 days after the Attorney General's written notice (§ 59.1-584 B)

evidence.quote: may seek an injunction to restrain any violations of this chapter

enforcement.triggered_by: Any action initiated under the chapter: recovery of reasonable investigation and preparation expenses, including attorney fees

evidence.quote: The Attorney General may recover reasonable expenses incurred in investigating and preparing the case, including attorney fees, in any action initiated under this chapter.

"Consumer" means a natural person who is a resident of the Commonwealth acting only in an individual or household context. It does not include a natural person acting in a commercial or employment context.
"Controller" means the natural or legal person that, alone or jointly with others, determines the purpose and means of processing personal data.
"Processor" means a natural or legal entity that processes personal data on behalf of a controller.

"Personal data" means any information that is linked or reasonably linkable to an identified or identifiable natural person. "Personal data" does not include de-identified data or publicly available information.
Personal data revealing racial or ethnic origin, religious beliefs, mental or physical health diagnosis, sexual orientation, or citizenship or immigration status

definitions.term: Sale of personal data (and exclusions: processors, requested services, affiliates, public disclosures, mergers)

evidence.quote: "Sale of personal data" means the exchange of personal data for monetary consideration by the controller to a third party.

definitions.term: Targeted advertising (and exclusions: first-party, contextual, requested, measurement)

evidence.quote: "Targeted advertising" means displaying advertisements to a consumer where the advertisement is selected based on personal data obtained from that consumer's activities over time and across nonaffiliated websites or online applications to predict such consumer's preferences or interests.

"Profiling" means any form of automated processing performed on personal data to evaluate, analyze, or predict personal aspects related to an identified or identifiable natural person's economic situation, health, personal preferences, interests, reliability, behavior, location, or movements.

definitions.term: Decisions that produce legal or similarly significant effects concerning a consumer

evidence.quote: "Decisions that produce legal or similarly significant effects concerning a consumer" means a decision made by the controller that results in the provision or denial by the controller of financial and lending services, housing, insurance, education enrollment, criminal justice, employment opportunities, health care services, or access to basic necessities, such as food and water.
"Consent" means a clear affirmative act signifying a consumer's freely given, specific, informed, and unambiguous agreement to process personal data relating to the consumer.
"Child" means any natural person younger than 13 years of age.
For purposes of this section, "minor" means any natural person younger than 16 years of age.
"Social media platform" means a public or semipublic Internet-based service or application that has users in the Commonwealth and that meets the following criteria:
"Online service, product, or feature" means any service, product, or feature that is provided online.

"Biometric data" means data generated by automatic measurements of an individual's biological characteristics, such as a fingerprint, voiceprint, eye retinas, irises, or other unique biological patterns or characteristics that is used to identify a specific individual.

"Precise geolocation data" means information derived from technology, including but not limited to global positioning system level latitude and longitude coordinates or other mechanisms, that directly identifies the specific location of a natural person with precision and accuracy within a radius of 1,750 feet.
"De-identified data" means data that cannot reasonably be linked to an identified or identifiable natural person, or a device linked to such person.
"Pseudonymous data" means personal data that cannot be attributed to a specific natural person without the use of additional information
"Publicly available information" means information that is lawfully made available through federal, state, or local government records
"Affiliate" means a legal entity that controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with another legal entity or shares common branding with another legal entity.
"Third party" means a natural or legal person, public authority, agency, or body other than the consumer, controller, processor, or an affiliate of the processor or the controller.

"Nonprofit organization" means any corporation organized under the Virginia Nonstock Corporation Act (§ 13.1-801 et seq.) or any organization exempt from taxation under § 501(c)(3), 501(c)(6), or 501(c)(12) of the Internal Revenue Code
"Institution of higher education" means a public institution and private institution of higher education, as those terms are defined in § 23.1-100.
"Covered entity" means the same as the term is established by HIPAA.
"Health record" means the same as that term is defined in § 32.1-127.1:03.

relations.note: Data protection assessments are confidential and exempt from public inspection under FOIA

evidence.quote: Data protection assessments shall be confidential and exempt from public inspection and copying under the Virginia Freedom of Information Act (§ 2.2-3700 et seq.).

entities.name: Attorney General of Virginia
entities.function: Exclusive enforcement authority; issues 30-day cure notices, civil investigative demands; may request and evaluate data protection assessments; receives consumer complaints after denied appeals

evidence.quote: The Attorney General shall have exclusive authority to enforce the provisions of this chapter.

entities.name: Regulatory, Consumer Advocacy, Litigation, and Enforcement Revolving Trust Fund
entities.function: Receives civil penalties, expenses and attorney fees collected under the chapter

evidence.quote: All civil penalties, expenses, and attorney fees collected pursuant to this chapter shall be paid into the state treasury and credited to the Regulatory, Consumer Advocacy, Litigation, and Enforcement Revolving Trust Fund.

notes: Scope: § 59.1-576 B excludes public bodies, GLBA financial institutions, HIPAA covered entities and business associates, nonprofit organizations and institutions of higher education; § 59.1-576 C lists 14 exempt data categories (health, research, FCRA, DPPA, FERPA, Farm Credit Act, employment and emergency-contact data). § 59.1-578 B voids contract terms that waive or limit consumer rights (not coded as an obligation). § 59.1-582 lists permitted processing that the chapter does not restrict (legal compliance, security and fraud, internal research, product recalls, etc.) and § 59.1-582 D shields a disclosing controller or processor from a recipient's violations absent actual knowledge. § 59.1-584 E states there is no private right of action 'for violations of this chapter or under any other law'. The 25,000-consumer prong of § 59.1-576 A (ii) is not tied to 'during a calendar year' in the text, unlike prong (i); read literally, as coded. Effective dates of Acts 2025 c. 703 (§ 59.1-577.1) and Acts 2026 c. 820 (§ 59.1-578 A 6) are unknown here (session laws not retrieved, access log), so the related obligations have applies_from null. That § 59.1-578 F and § 59.1-580 B were added by Acts 2024 cc. 840, 844 is inferred from their absence in the 2021 and 2022 session-law texts. Legislative events cite SB 1392 only; the companion HB 2307 history was not checked. The registry date 'adopted' 2021-03-02 corresponds to the Governor's approval (coded 'signed').
